semin-durr:3-3.t:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
His saying: {عَمَّآ أُنذِرُواْ}: «ما» may be a maṣdar particle, i.e. "away from their being warned," or have the sense of "that which," i.e. "away from that of which they were warned." «عن» is attached to the turning away, and «مُعْرِضون» is the khabar of the relative noun.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {أَرَأَيْتُمْ}: its ruling has been given. «أَرُوْني» occurs after it, so it admits two aspects. The first: it is emphasis of it, because both mean "tell me." On this basis, the second object of «أَرَأَيْتُمْ» is His saying «ماذا خَلَقوا», because it is an interrogative, and the first object is His saying «ما تَدْعُون». The second aspect: it is not emphasis of it. On this basis the question is of the chapter of mutual contention (tanāzuʿ), because «أَرَأَيْتُمْ» requires a second object, and «أرُوْني» likewise, and His saying «ماذا خَلَقوا» is the thing contended over; and the question is one of applying the second verb's operation, with omission from the first. Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed that «أَرَأَيْتُم» not be transitive, and made «ما تَدْعُوْن» an interrogative whose meaning is reproach. He said: "«تَدْعُوْنَ» means 'you worship.'" I say: this is the opinion of al-Akhfash, and he said so regarding His saying: {قَالَ أَرَأَيْتَ إِذْ أَوَيْنَآ إِلَى الصخرة} [al-Kahf: 63], and that has passed.
His saying: «من الأرض»: this is the clarification of the vagueness in His saying «ماذا خَلَقُوا».
His saying: «أَمْ لهم»: this is the disconnected «أم». And الشِّرْك means partnership.
His saying: {مِّن قَبْلِ هاذآ}: an adjective of «كتاب», i.e. "with a book sent down before this." Abū l-Baqāʾ implied it so. It is better to imply/ an absolute being, i.e. "existing before this."
His saying: «أَو أَثَارَةٍ»: the majority read «أَثارة», which is a maṣdar on the pattern fa ʿāla, like السَّماحَة, الغَواية and الضَّلالة, and its meaning is "remnant," from their saying: "the she-camel became fat on a remnant (athāra) of flesh," when she was fat, then grew lean, and a remnant of her fat remained, then she grew fat. The use of الأثارة predominantly applies to the remnant of nobility. One says: "So-and-so has an athāra," i.e. a remnant of nobility, and it is used in other senses. al-Rāʿī said:
وذاتِ أثارَةٍ أكلَتْ عليها ... نباتاً في أكِمَّتِهِ قِفارا
(And one with a remnant of flesh, on which she ate plants in its desolate hills.)
It is also said that its derivation is from أَثَر كذا, i.e. he traced it back (asnadahu). From it comes the saying of ʿUmar: "I have not sworn, whether reporting from myself or transmitting (āthiran)," i.e. attributing it to someone else. al-Aʿshā said:
4039 - أإنَّ الذي فيه تَمارَيْتُما ... بُيِّنَ للسامعِ والآثِرِ
(Indeed that over which you two disputed has been made clear to the hearer and to the transmitter.)
Other things have been said about it. ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, Zayd ibn ʿAlī and ʿIkrima, among others, read «أَثَرَة» without alif, which is the singular. It is pluralised as أَثَر, like قَتَرَة and قَتَر. al-Kisāʾī read «أُثْرَة» and «إثْرَة», with ḍamma and kasra on the hamza respectively, and sukūn on the thāʾ. Qatāda and al-Sulamī read it with fatḥa and sukūn. The meaning is: "by what is transmitted and narrated," i.e. "bring me a single report that testifies to the soundness of your claim." This is by way of descending (to their level), given the knowledge that the claimant is lying. And «مِن عِلْمٍ» is an adjective of «أَثارة».
[Translator's note: the source numbers the verse of al-Aʿshā here 4039 and the verse in the next entries of this surah, 46:9, is also numbered 4039; the verse of al-Rāʿī above is unnumbered in the source. Reproduced as printed.]

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {وَمَنْ أَضَلُّ}: mubtadaʾ and khabar.
His saying: {مَن لاَّ يَسْتَجِيبُ}: «مَنْ» is an indefinite described or a relative, and it is the object of «يَدْعُو».
His saying: {وَهُمْ عَن دُعَآئِهِمْ}: the two pronouns may refer back to «مَنْ» in His saying {مَن لاَّ يَسْتَجِيبُ لَهُ}, which are the idols, and «مَنْ» is applied to them because they treat them as they treat rational beings, or because he meant everything worshipped besides Allah and gave priority to the rational; and so he has regarded the meaning of «مَنْ», therefore it is plural in His saying «وهم», after having regarded its wording, so it is singular in His saying «يَسْتَجيب». It is also said that it refers back to «مَنْ» in His saying «ومَنْ أضَلُّ», and it was first carried according to its wording, so it is singular in His saying «يَدْعُو», then according to its meaning, so it is plural in His saying {وَهُمْ عَن دُعَآئِهِمْ غَافِلُونَ}.

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {قَالَ الذين كَفَرُواْ لِلْحَقِّ}: here he put two overt nouns in the place of two pronouns; for the original is "they said of it," i.e. of the verses, but he made them overt because of the two attributes mentioned. The lām in «للحق» is for cause.

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {بِدْعاً}: there are two aspects. The first: with an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being "possessor of novelty" (dhā bidʿ); Abū l-Baqāʾ said this. This is on the basis that al-bidʿ is a maṣdar. The second: al-bidʿ is itself an adjective on the pattern fiʿl in the sense of badīʿ, like al-khiff and al-khafīf. al-Bidʿ and al-badīʿ mean what has not been seen to have an equal, and it is from ibtidāʿ, which is invention. Quṭrub recited:
4039 - فما أنا بِدْعٌ مِنْ حوادِثَ تَعْتَري ... رجالاً عَرَتْ مِنْ بعدِ بُؤْسَى بأَسْعُدِ
(I am no novelty among the misfortunes that befall men, which befell after Buʾsā with Asʿud.)
ʿIkrima, Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «بِدَعاً» with fatḥa on the dāl, the plural of بِدْعة, i.e. "you were not the possessor of novelties." al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be an adjective on the pattern fiʿal, like «دِين قِيَم» and «لحم زِيَم». The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "Sībawayh did not establish an adjective on the pattern fiʿal except «قوماً عِدَا», and «لحم زِيَم», i.e. scattered, was added against him, and it is sound. As for «قِيَم», it is a shortened form of قيام, and were it not so, its ʿayn would have remained sound as it remained in حِوَل and عِوَض. As for the saying of the Arabs «مكان سِوَىً», «ماء رِوَىً», «رجل رِضَا» and «ماء صِرَىً», these are interpreted according to the morphologists." I say: their interpretation is either as maṣdars or by shortening, like قِيَم for قيام.
Abū Ḥaywa also read, and Mujāhid, «بِدَع» with fatḥa on the bāʾ and kasra on the dāl, which is an adjective like حَذِر.
His saying: «يُفْعَلُ»: the majority read it in the passive. Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it in the active, i.e. Allah the Exalted. The apparent view is that «ما» in His saying {مَا يُفْعَلُ بِي} is interrogative, nominative through the inceptive, with what follows it as the khabar, and it suspends «أَدْري» from operating, so it stands in for its two objects. al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be a relative in the accusative, meaning that it is transitive to one object, i.e. "I do not know that which Allah the Exalted does."
His saying: {إِلاَّ مَا يوحى}: the majority read «يُوحَى» in the passive. Ibn ʿUmayr read it with kasra on the ḥāʾ, in the active, the agent being Allah the Exalted.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ}: its two objects are omitted, the implied form being "Have you considered your state, if it was such, are you not wrongdoers?"/ and the apodosis of the condition is also omitted, its implied form being "then you have done wrong"; therefore he put the verb of the condition in the past. al-Zamakhsharī implied it as "are you not wrongdoers?" The Shaykh rejected him: "Because if it were so, the fāʾ would be obligatory, since an interrogative clause, whenever it falls as the apodosis of a condition, must take the fāʾ. Then if the interrogative particle is a hamza, it precedes the fāʾ, as in: 'If you visit us, do we not honour you?'; and if it is other than that, the fāʾ precedes it, as in: 'If you visit us, do you see anything but good?'" I say: al-Zamakhsharī mentioned an implied matter by which he explained the meaning, not the i'rab.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«أَرَأَيْتُمْ» may be an alerter, so it is a word set down for questioning that does not require an object; and it may be that the clause «كان» and what it operates on stands in for its two objects." The Shaykh said: "This is contrary to what the grammarians established." I say: the verification of what they established has been given. It is also said: the apodosis of the condition is His saying «فآمَن واستكْبَرْتُمْ». It is also said: it is omitted, its implied form being "who then is in the right among us, and who in the wrong?" And it is said: "who then is more astray?"
His saying: «وكَفَرْتُمْ به»: the clause is a ḥāl, i.e. "and you have disbelieved." Some do not imply «قد» in the like of it.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ}: it may be the lām of cause, i.e. "for their sake," or it may be for conveyance. Had they followed what the address requires, they would have said "you did not precede us," but they turned to the third person and said "they did not precede us." The pronouns in «كان» and «إليه» refer back to the Qur'an, or to what the Messenger brought.
His saying: {وَإِذْ لَمْ يَهْتَدُواْ}: the operator in «إذْ» is implied, i.e. "their stubbornness appeared, and His saying «فسَيقولون» results from it." «فسَيقولون» cannot operate on «إذ», because of the opposition of the two times, and also because of the fāʾ.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {وَمِن قَبْلِهِ كِتَابُ موسى}: the majority read the mīm of «مِنْ» with kasra, as a preposition. It with its genitive noun is a fronted khabar. The clause is a ḥāl or a resumptive khabar.
al-Kalbī read «الكتابَ» accusative, its implied form being "and He sent down before it the Book of Moses." It was also read «ومَنْ» with fatḥa on the mīm and «كتابَ موسى» accusative, on the basis that «مَنْ» is a relative, the first object of an implied «آتَيْنا», and «كتابَ موسى» its second object, i.e. "and We gave the one before it the Book of Moses."
His saying: «إماماً ورَحْمَةً»: two ḥāls from «كتاب موسى». It is also said they are accusative through an implied verb, i.e. "We sent it down as a guide"; there is no need for it. On their being two ḥāls, they are accusative by what «مِن قبل» is accusative by, namely the settled-in-place meaning.
His saying: «لِساناً»: a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مُصَدِّقٌ». It may also be a ḥāl from «كتاب», the operator being the alerting or the sense of pointing; and «عربيَّاً» is an adjective of «لساناً», and it is what justifies this inert noun falling as a ḥāl. Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed it to be a direct object, governed by «مُصَدِّقٌ». On this basis the pointing is to something other than the Qur'an, because by "Arabic tongue" is meant the Qur'an, which is contrary to the apparent view. It is also said to be with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "confirming the possessor of an Arabic tongue," who is the Prophet ﷺ. It is also said to be with removal of the preposition, i.e. "in a tongue," which is weak.
His saying: «ليُنْذِرَ»: attached to «مصدِّق». And «بُشْرَى» is conjoined to its position, its implied form being "for warning and for glad tidings," and since the cause and the effect differ, the operator reaches it by the lām [this applies to whoever read with the second-person tāʾ. As for whoever read with the third-person yāʾ, and that was given earlier in Yā Sīn, the two are the same. It is also said: «بُشْرى»] is conjoined to the wording of «لتنذِرَ», i.e. it is genitive only. It is also said it is nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "it is glad tidings." It is also said that it is conjoined to «مُصَدِّقٌ». And it is said it is accusative through an implied verb, i.e. "and give glad tidings." The Shaykh related the accusative aspect, conjunction upon the position of «لتنذِرَ», from al-Zamakhsharī and Abū l-Baqāʾ. Then he said: "This is not sound according to the sound view among the grammarians' schools, because they stipulate for carrying onto the position that it be by right of originality, and that the place have a secure basis, and here the position is not by right of originality, since the original in the mafʿūl lahu is the genitive, and the accusative arises from it, but when it became frequent, with the stipulated conditions, the verb reached it and made it accusative." End quotation.
His saying "the original in the mafʿūl lahu is the genitive by the particle" is not conceded, by the proof of the grammarians' saying that it is accusative on conditions which they mentioned. Then they say: "and it may be made genitive with a lām"; so their saying "it may" is apparently a sign that it is a secondary form, not an original.
And «للمُحْسِنين» is attached to «بُشْرَى» or to an omitted element as an adjective of it.

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {فَلاَ خَوْفٌ}: the fāʾ is redundant in the khabar of the relative noun, because of the sense of condition in it, and «إنَّ» does not prevent that because the sense of the inceptive remains, unlike «ليت», «لعلَّ» and «كأن».

semin-durr:14-14.t: His saying: {خَالِدِينَ}: accusative as a ḥāl. And «جزاءً» is accusative as a maṣdar, either through an implied operator, i.e. "they are recompensed a recompense," or through what preceded, because the meaning of «أولئك أصحاب الجنة» is the meaning of "We recompensed them with that."

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying: {إِحْسَاناً}: the Kufans read «إحْساناً» and the rest of the seven read «حُسْناً» with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ and sukūn on the sīn. On the first reading, «إحساناً» is accusative through an implied verb, i.e. "We enjoined him to do good to them both, a doing of good." It is also said: rather it is a direct object by containing in «وصَّيْنا» the sense of "We obliged," so it is a second object. It is also said: rather it is accusative as a direct object, i.e. "We enjoined him concerning them kindness from us toward them." It is also said: it is accusative as a maṣdar, because the meaning of «وصَّيْنا» is "We did good," so it is a pure maṣdar. And the second object / is what is genitive through the bāʾ. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is attached either to «وَصَّيْنا» or to «إحساناً»." The Shaykh rejected this second: it is an interpreted maṣdar, so what it governs cannot precede it; and «أَحْسَنَ» is not made transitive with the bāʾ, only with the lām; you do not say "aḥsantu bi-Zayd" in the sense of the arrival of goodness to him. Some have rejected this with His saying: {وَقَدْ أَحْسَنَ بي إِذْ أَخْرَجَنِي} [Yūsuf: 100]; and it is said that it is in a different sense. Some implied: "We enjoined man concerning his parents, as one possessed of good conduct," meaning it is a ḥāl. As for «حُسْناً», what was said under «إحسان» is said of it.
ʿĪsā and al-Sulamī read «حَسَناً» with fatḥa on both. The meaning of the two readings was given in al-Baqara and in Luqmān.
His saying: «كُرْهاً»: the disagreement about it has been given in al-Nisāʾ. And in it (the question whether) they are of one meaning or not. [Translator's note: the source wording here is «وله هما بمعنىً واحد أم لا؟»; translated as printed, and it appears to be garbled.] Abū Ḥātim said: "الكَرْه with fatḥa is not good, because with fatḥa it means force and compulsion." What he said is not heeded, given the mutawātir status of this reading. Its accusative is either as a ḥāl from the agent, i.e. "possessing reluctance," or as an adjective of an implied maṣdar, i.e. "a reluctant bearing."
His saying: «وحَمْلُه», i.e. the period of his bearing. The majority read «فِصالُه», a maṣdar of فاصَلَ, as if the mother separated from him and he from her. al-Jaḥdarī, al-Ḥasan and Qatāda read «فَصْلُه». It is said: الفَصْل and الفِصال mean the same, like الفَطْم and الفِطام, and القَطْف and القِطاف. Had «ثلاثين» been made accusative as an adverbial occurring in the place of the khabar, it would have been permitted, and it is the original. This is when we do not imply a muḍāf; if we do, i.e. "the period of his bearing," that is not permitted and the nominative is required, because the khabar and what is reported about are coextensive.
His saying: {حتى إِذَا بَلَغَ}: an omitted clause is needed for which «حتى» is the end-point, i.e. "he lived and his life continued until, when…"
His saying: «أربعين»: i.e. its completion, so «أربعين» is a direct object.
His saying: {وَأَصْلِحْ لِي فِي ذريتي}: أَصْلَحَ is transitive by itself, per His saying: {وَأَصْلَحْنَا لَهُ زَوْجَهُ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 90]; it is transitivised with «في» only because it contains the sense of "be kind to me in my offspring," or because he made the offspring a container of righteousness, like the saying:
4040 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . يَجْرَحُ في عَراقيبها نَصْلي
(… my blade wounds in their hamstrings.)

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {نَتَقَبَّلُ}: the two companions (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Ḥafṣ read «نَتَقَبَّلُ» with fatḥa on the nūn, active, with «أَحْسَنَ» accusative as direct object, and likewise «ونتجاوَزُ». The others read both passive, with «أحسنُ» nominative as it stands in for the agent, and with a yāʾ with ḍamma in place of the nūn in both verbs. al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿmash and ʿĪsā read with the yāʾ (below), the agent being Allah the Exalted.
His saying: {في أَصْحَابِ الجنة}: several aspects. The first, which is the apparent one: it is in the position of a ḥāl, i.e. "being among the people of Paradise," like your saying "the emir honoured me among his companions," i.e. among their number. The second: «في» is in the sense of «مع». The third: it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are among the people of Paradise."
His saying: «وَعْدَ الصدقِ»: an emphatic maṣdar of the content of the preceding clause, because His saying {أولئك الذين نَتَقَبَّلُ عَنْهُمْ} is in the sense of a promise.

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {أُفٍّ}: the discussion of «أُفّ» has been given in full, and «لكما» is a clarification, i.e. the saying "uff" is for you two, like {هَيْتَ} [Yūsuf: 23].
His saying: «أَتَعِدانِني»: the majority read it with two nūns with kasra: the first for the nominative and the second for protection (wiqāya); Hishām assimilated them, and Nāfiʿ in one transmission read with a single nūn. This is likened to His saying: {تأمروني أَعْبُدُ} [al-Zumar: 64]. al-Ḥasan, Shayba, Abū Jaʿfar and ʿAbd al-Wārith from Abū ʿAmr read the first nūn with fatḥa, as if they fled from the succession of two kasra-bearing like letters followed by a yāʾ. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is an irregular dialect, the fatḥa of the dual nūn." I say: if he means the dual nūn in nouns, as in the saying:
4041 - على أَحْوَذِيَّيْنَ اسْتَقَلَّتْ. . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(On two swift ones she rose… )
that is not this. If he means in the verb, that has not been established as a dialect, and the fatḥa here is only for what I mentioned.
His saying: «أَنْ أُخْرَجَ»: it is what is promised, so one may imply the bāʾ before «أَنْ» or not imply it.
His saying: «وقد خَلَتْ»: a circumstantial clause. Likewise {وَهُمَا يَسْتَغثِيَانِ الله}, i.e. "they ask Allah." اسْتَغاثَ is transitive by itself at times and with the bāʾ at others, although Ibn Mālik claimed it is transitive by itself only, and faulted the grammarians' "mustaghāth bihi." I say: but it has not occurred in the Qur'an except transitive by itself: {إِذْ تَسْتَغِيثُونَ رَبَّكُمْ} [al-Anfāl: 9], {فاستغاثه الذي} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 15], {وَإِن يَسْتَغِيثُواْ يُغَاثُواْ} [al-Kahf: 29]. His saying: «وَيْلَكَ»: accusative as a maṣdar through a verb that meets it in meaning, not in derivation. Likewise: وَيْحَه, وَيْسَه and وَيْبَه. Or as a direct object, with the implied form "Allah impose upon you your woe." On both implications the clause is governed by an implied saying, i.e. "they say: woe to you, believe!" And the saying is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "they implore Allah, saying that."
His saying: {إِنَّ وَعْدَ الله حَقٌّ}: the majority read «إنَّ» with kasra, / as resumptive or causal. ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid and al-Aʿraj read it with fatḥa, governed by «آمِنْ» with the bāʾ omitted, i.e. "believe that the promise of Allah is true."

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {في أُمَمٍ}: like His saying: {في أَصْحَابِ الجنة} [al-Aḥqāf: 16].

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {وَلِيُوَفِّيَهُمْ}: what it justifies is omitted, its implied form being "He recompensed them with that." Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and Hishām read with the yāʾ (below). The rest of the seven read with the nūn. al-Sulamī read with the tāʾ (above), ascribing the full payment to the degrees figuratively.
His saying: {وَهُمْ لاَ يُظْلَمُونَ}: either resumptive or an emphatic ḥāl.

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying: {وَيَوْمَ يُعْرَضُ}: «اليومَ» is accusative through an implied saying, i.e. "it is said to them: you squandered, on the day of their being displayed." al-Zamakhsharī made this like "I displayed the she-camel to the water trough," so it would be an inversion (qalb). The Shaykh rejected him: it is a necessity (of poetry). Also, displaying is a relative matter, so its attribution to the she-camel and to the trough are both sound. The discussion of inversion has been given, and that there are three schools about it.
His saying: «أَذْهَبْتُم»: Ibn Kathīr read «أَأَذْهَبْتُمْ» with two hamzas, the first lightened and the second eased between the two (bayna bayna), without inserting an alif between them, and this is on his principle in {أَأَنذَرْتَهُمْ} [al-Baqara: 6] and the like. Ibn ʿĀmir also read with two hamzas, but his two transmitters differed from him: Hishām eased the second and also lightened it, and inserted an alif in both aspects, though this is not on his principle, for he is of the people of taḥqīq. Ibn Dhakwān read with taḥqīq only, without inserting an alif. The others read with a single hamza, which is either a statement or an interrogative whose particle was dropped because of an indication to it; and the interrogative means rebuke and reproach.
His saying: «في حياتِكم»: it may be attached to «أَذْهَبْتُمْ», and it may be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «طيباتكم».

semin-durr:21-21.t:
His saying: {إِذْ أَنذَرَ}: a badal of inclusion from «أَخا»; its verification has been given. الأَحْقاف is the plural of حِقْف, which is the long, curved sand dune; from it comes "the crescent became bent" (iḥqawqafa). Imruʾ al-Qays said:
4042 - فلمَّا أَجَزْنا ساحةَ الحيِّ وانتحى ... بنا بَطْنُ حِقْفٍ ذي قِفافٍ عَقَنْقَلِ
(When we passed the tribe's encampment, and the heart of a dune with ridges and tangled sands turned us aside.)
His saying: «وقد خَلَتْ»: it may be a ḥāl from the agent or from the object, the link being the wāw. النُّذُر is the plural of نَذير. It may also be parenthetical between «أَنْذَرَ» and {أَلاَّ تعبدوا}, i.e. "he warned them that they not…"

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying: {فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ عَارِضاً}: there are two sayings about the hāʾ of «رَأَوْه». The first: it refers back to «ما تَعِدُنا». The second: it is a vague pronoun which «عارضاً» explains, either as tamyīz or as ḥāl; al-Zamakhsharī said both. The Shaykh rejected him: the tamyīz that explains a pronoun is restricted to the chapter of «رُبَّ» and «نِعْمَ» and «بِئْس», and a ḥāl is not known to clarify a pronoun before it, and the grammarians do not know that.
His saying: «مُسْتَقْبِلَ أَوْدِيَتِهم»: an adjective of «عارِضاً», and its annexation is not pure (ghayr maḥḍa), and therefore it was permissible for it to be an adjective of an indefinite; likewise «مُمْطِرُنا» occurs as an adjective of «عارِض». Similar is:
4043 - يا رُبَّ غابِطِنا لو كان يَطْلُبُكُمْ ... لاقى مباعَدَةً منكم وحِرْمانا
(O many an envier of us who, had he sought you, would have met distance and deprivation from you.)
العارِض is the cloud that spans across the sky. He said:
4044 - يا مَنْ رَأَى عارِضاً أَرِقْتُ له ... بين ذراعَيْ وجَبْهَةِ الأَسَدِ
(O you who saw a cloud for which I lay awake, between the two arms and the brow of the Lion.)
It has been given earlier that أَوْدِيَة is the plural of «وادٍ», and that the pattern afʿila is irregular as a plural of fāʿil in some words: such as وادٍ and أَوْدِيَة, نادٍ and أَنْدِية, جائِز and أَجْوِزة.
His saying: «ريحٌ»: it may be the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is a wind," or a badal from «هو». «ما استُعْجِلْتُمْ» was also read in the passive. «وفيها عذابٌ» is an adjective of «ريحٌ», and likewise «تُدَمِّرُ». {يَدْمُرُ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ} was also read with yāʾ (below), sukūn on the dāl and ḍamma on the mīm, with «كلُّ» nominative as the agent, i.e. "everything perishes." Zayd ibn ʿAlī likewise, except with tāʾ (above) and «كلَّ» accusative, the agent being the pronoun of the wind; on this the triliteral دَمَّر is both intransitive and transitive.

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {فَأْصْبَحُواْ لاَ يرى إِلاَّ مَسَاكِنُهُمْ}: Ḥamza and ʿĀṣim read «لا يُرَى» with ḍamma on the yāʾ (below), passive, with «مَسَاكنُهم» nominative as it stands in for the agent. The rest of the seven read with the second-person tāʾ with fatḥa, «مَساكنَهم» accusative as direct object. al-Jaḥdarī, al-Aʿmash, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, al-Sulamī and Abū Rajāʾ read with ḍamma on the tāʾ (above), passive, «مساكنُهم» nominative as it stands in for the agent, except that this is not permitted according to the majority, I mean when the separator is «إلاَّ», for the attachment of the feminine mark to the verb is prevented except in necessity, as in the saying: /
4045 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وما بَقِيَتْ إلاَّ الضلوعُ الجراشِعُ
(… and nothing remained except the broad-chested ribs.)
and the saying of another:
4046 - كأنه جَمَلٌ هَمٌّ وما بَقِيَتْ ... إلاَّ النَّحِيزةُ والألواحُ والعَصَبُ
(As if he were a worn-out camel, and nothing remained except the nature, the planks (bones) and the sinews.)
ʿĪsā al-Hamdānī read «لا يُرى» with yāʾ (below), passive, «مَسْكَنُهم» singular. Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim read with the second-person tāʾ, «مَسْكَنَهم» also singular and accusative; the singular was made to suffice for the plural.

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying: {مَآ إِن مَّكَّنَّاكُمْ فِيهِ}: «ما» is a relative or an indefinite described. There are three aspects regarding «إنْ»: conditional, with its apodosis omitted, and the conditional clause is the ṣila of «ما», the implied form being "in that in which, if We established you, you transgressed." The second: it is redundant, in likening the relative «ما» to the negative «ما» and the temporal «ما». This is like the saying:
4047 - يُرَجِّي المرءُ ما إنْ لا يَراهُ ... وتَعرِضُ دونَ أَدْناه الخُطوبُ
(A man hopes for what he may not see, and calamities intervene before the nearest of it.)
The third, which is the sound one: it is negative, in the sense: "We established them in that in which We did not establish you, of strength, stature and breadth of provisions." The saying of the Exalted in several places indicates it: {كانوا أَشَدَّ مِنْهُمْ قُوَّةً} [al-Rūm: 9] and the like. He departed from the word negative «ما» to «إنْ» only out of dislike of the meeting of two identical words. al-Zamakhsharī said: "Abū l-Ṭayyib (al-Mutanabbī) made it insipid in his saying:
4048 - لَعَمْرُك ما ما بان منك لِضاربٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(By your life, what [what] became manifest from you to a striker… )
What would it have harmed him had he followed the sweetness of the wording of the revelation and said «ما إنْ بانَ منك»?"
His saying: «فما أَغْنى»: «ما» may be negation, which is the apparent view, or an interrogative of affirmation. The Shaykh considered the latter unlikely because of His saying «مِنْ شيء». He said: "Because the implied form would become 'what thing availed them in the slightest,' so «مِنْ» would be added in the affirmative, which is not permitted on the sound view." I say: they said that its addition is permitted in the non-affirmative, and they explained the non-affirmative as negation, prohibition and interrogation, and this is an interrogative.
His saying: «إذ كانوا»: governed by «أَغْنى», and it carries a tinge of the meaning of cause, i.e. "because they were denying."

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying: {قُرْبَاناً آلِهَةَ}: four aspects. The most probable: the first object of «اتَّخذوا» is omitted, being the returning pronoun of the relative; «قُرْباناً» is accusative as a ḥāl, and «آلهةً» is the second object of the taking. The implied form: "Why did those whom they took as gods, as a means of drawing near by them, not help them?" The second: the first object is omitted, as stated, «قُرْباناً» is the second object and «آلهةً» a badal from it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya, al-Ḥūfī and Abū l-Baqāʾ inclined to it. But al-Zamakhsharī prevented this aspect, saying: "because of corruption of the meaning," and did not make clear the aspect of the corruption. The Shaykh said: "It appears that the meaning is sound on that i'rab." I say: the aspect of the corruption, and Allah knows best, is that qurbān is a name for what is used to draw near to the deity; so if we made it a second object, and «آلهةً» a badal from it, it would follow that the thing used for drawing near is gods, whereas the supposition is that it is other than the gods, rather it is something by which one draws near to them, so it is other than them; so how could the gods be a badal for it? This is not permitted. The third: «قُرْباناً» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi; the Shaykh attributed it to al-Ḥūfī. I say: Abū l-Baqāʾ also took this view, and on this «آلهةً» is a second object and the first is omitted as stated. The fourth: that it is a maṣdar; Makkī related it. Were it not that he mentioned a second aspect, the mafʿūl li-ajlihi, I would have interpreted his statement as meaning by "maṣdar" the mafʿūl li-ajlihi, given the remoteness of the sense of maṣdar.
His saying: «إفْكُهم»: the majority read it with kasra on the hamza and sukūn on the fāʾ, a maṣdar of أَفَكَ يَأْفِك إفْكاً, i.e. "their lying." Ibn ʿAbbās read it with fatḥa, which is also a maṣdar of it. Ibn ʿAbbās also, ʿIkrima and al-Ṣabbāḥ ibn al-ʿAlāʾ read «أَفَكَهُمْ» with three fatḥas, a past verb, i.e. "he turned them away." Abū ʿIyāḍ and ʿIkrima also read likewise except with shadda on the fāʾ for multiplication. Ibn al-Zubayr and Ibn ʿAbbās also read «آفَكَهم» with elongation, also a past verb, and it may be on the pattern fāʿala, in which case the hamza is original, or on the pattern afʿala, in which case the hamza is added and the second is a substitute for a hamza. If we say it is afʿala, its hamza may be for transitivity, or afʿala may be in the sense of the bare form. Ibn ʿAbbās also read «آفِكُهم» with elongation, kasra on the fāʾ and nominative kāf, making it an active participle in the sense of "the one who turns them away." «أَفَكُهم» was also read with two fatḥas and nominative kāf, as a maṣdar of أَفَكَ too, so it would have three maṣdars: الأَفْك, الإِفْك (with fatḥa and with kasra on the hamza, with sukūn on the fāʾ) and with fatḥa on the hamza and the fāʾ. Abū l-Baqāʾ added that «آفَكُهم» was read with elongation, fatḥa on the fāʾ and nominative kāf. He said: "in the sense of 'the greatest liar among them'," making it an elative.
His saying: {وَمَا كَانُواْ يَفْتَرُونَ}: / «ما» may be a maṣdar particle, which is better so that it is conjoined to its like, or have the sense of "that which," with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "they used to fabricate." The maṣdar in His saying «إفْكُهم» may be annexed to the agent in the sense of "their lying," or to the object in the sense of "their being turned away."

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying: {وَإِذْ صَرَفْنَآ}: accusative through an implied "remember." «صَرَّفْنا» with shadda was also read, for multiplication. «من الجنِّ» is an adjective of «نَفَراً», and it may be attached to «صَرَفْنا», with «مِنْ» for the beginning of the range.
His saying: «يَسْتَمِعُون»: also an adjective of «نَفَراً», or a ḥāl because of its being specified by the adjective, if we say that «مِنَ الجنِّ» is an adjective of it; and he regarded the meaning of «النَّفر», so he returned the pronoun to it in the plural; had he regarded its wording and said «يَسْتمع», it would have been permissible.
His saying: «فلَمَّا حَضَرُوْه»: the hāʾ may be for the Qur'an, which is the apparent view, or for the Messenger, peace be upon him, in which case there is an iltifāt (shift of person) in the speech from His saying «إليك» to the third person in His saying «حَضَرُوه».
His saying: «قُضِي»: the majority read it passive, i.e. the recitation of the Qur'an was finished, which supports the hāʾ of «حَضَروه» referring to the Qur'an. Abū Mijlaz and Ḥabīb ibn ʿAbd Allāh read «قَضَى» active, i.e. the Messenger completed his recitation, and this supports its referring to the Messenger, peace be upon him.

semin-durr:31-31.t: His saying: {مِّن ذُنُوبِكُمْ}: it may be partitive, or redundant according to those who hold that view.

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying: {وَلَمْ يَعْيَ}: the majority read it with sukūn on the ʿayn and fatḥa on the yāʾ, the imperfect of عَيِيَ (with kasra) يَعْيا (with fatḥa); when the jussive particle entered, the alif was dropped. al-Ḥasan read «يَعِيْ» with kasra on the ʿayn and sukūn on the yāʾ. They said: its original is عَيِيَ with kasra; he turned the kasra into fatḥa in the dialect of Ṭayyiʾ, so it became «عَيا», as they said of بَقِيَ: بَقَا. When the past was built on faʿala with fatḥa, its imperfect came on yafʿilu with kasra, so it became يَعْيِي like يَرْمي. When the jussive entered, the second yāʾ was dropped, so it became «لم يَعْيِ» with a sukūn ʿayn and a kasra yāʾ; then the vowel of the yāʾ was moved to the ʿayn, so the word became as you see. It has already been given that عَيِيَ and حَيِيَ have two dialectal forms: unassimilated and assimilated. As for «حِيِي», it was given in al-Anfāl. And عَيَّ is as in the saying:
4049 - عَيُّوا بأَمْرِهِمُ كما ... عَيَّتْ ببَيْضَتِها الحمَامَهْ
(They were at a loss over their affair, as the dove is at a loss over its egg.)
And العِيّ is the failure to find the way to a direction. From it comes العِيّ in speech, and "he was at a loss about the matter" when he did not find its way.
His saying: «بقادرٍ»: the bāʾ is redundant. What makes its redundancy good is that the speech has the force of "Is Allah not able?"; al-Zajjāj analogised "I did not think anyone was standing (bi-qāʾim)" to it, but the sound view is to withhold judgement. ʿĪsā, Zayd ibn ʿAlī and al-Jaḥdarī read «يَقْدِرُ», the imperfect of قَدَرَ, and the orthography admits it. His saying «بلى» is an affirmation of what the speech contains of negation in His saying {أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ}.

semin-durr:34-34.t: His saying: {أَلَيْسَ هذا}: governed by an implied saying which is a ḥāl, as given for its parallel earlier.

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying: {فاصبر}: the fāʾ conjoins this clause to what preceded, and the causal sense in it is apparent.
His saying: «من الرسُل»: it may be partitive, and on that the messengers are those of resolve and those not of resolve. It may be explicative, and on that all of them are of resolve.
His saying: «بلاغٌ»: the majority read it nominative. There are two aspects. The first: it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; some implied "that hour is a delivery (of the message)," from the indication of His saying {إِلاَّ سَاعَةً مِّن نَّهَارٍ}. It is also said that the implied form is "this," i.e. the Qur'an and the law, "is a delivery." The second: it is a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is His saying «لهم», which occurs after His saying «ولا تَسْتَعْجِلْ», i.e. "for them is a delivery," so one stops at «فلا تَسْتعجل». This is very weak because of the separation by the comparative clause, since the apparent view is that «لهم» is attached to the seeking haste, so it resembles making ready and cutting off. Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā read «بلاغاً» accusative as a maṣdar, i.e. "he delivered a delivery," and the reading of Abū Mijlaz «بَلِّغْ» as an imperative supports it. He also read «بَلَغَ» as a past verb.
From the speech of Makkī it is taken that its accusative as an adjective of «ساعةً» is permitted, for he said: "Were «بلاغاً» to be read accusative as a maṣdar or as an adjective of «ساعةً», it would be permitted." I say: it has been read so, and it seems he did not come across that.
al-Ḥasan also read «بلاغ» genitive. It was derived as an adjective of «نهار» with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "from a day of delivery," or the time was described by delivery for exaggeration.
His saying: «يُهْلَكُ»: the majority read it passive. Ibn Muḥayṣin read «يَهْلِك» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and kasra on the lām, active. From him also is fatḥa on the lām, which is a dialect; the past is هلِكَ with kasra. Ibn Jinnī said: "All of these are disfavoured." Zayd ibn Thābit read with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the lām, / the agent being Allah the Exalted, «القومَ الفاسقين» accusative as direct object. And «نُهْلك» with nūn and «القوم» accusative.
